For retirement investors seeking the cleanest way to own the AI infrastructure buildout, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) at $230.36 warrants a hard look, because the company is selling a product no rival can match at a price the market has not caught up to. China's best domestic AI chip, Huawei's Ascend 910C, tops out at roughly 780 teraflops (TFLOPS) of FP16 performance, less than half of the ~1,700 TFLOPS delivered by NVIDIA's H200, a chip unveiled nearly three years ago. While competitors chase that old benchmark, NVIDIA has moved through Blackwell, Blackwell Ultra, and into full production on Vera Rubin, whose single GPU delivers 4,000 TFLOPS of FP16 compute. That is the definition of a widening moat.

A forthcoming surge in demand for Intel's CPUs

The AI boom is creating a massive need for the semiconductor chips that power high-performance computing infrastructure. Many investors are aware of this trend. But they may be overlooking the shift toward central processor units (CPUs), as compute needs transition from graphics processing unit (GPU)-based model training to agentic AI workloads.

Global Equities Research analyst Trip Chowdhry believes this shift will help Intel's annual earnings per share grow more than tenfold to $20 by 2031. For context, Wall Street's consensus estimates call for Intel's EPS to increase to $1.51 in 2026 and $2.04 in 2027, as per Yahoo! Finance.

In turn, Chowdhry sees Intel's stock price more than doubling to $200 per share.

Dell's gains bode well for Intel

Chowdhry cites Dell's (NYSE: DELL) recent earnings release and subsequent management commentary as evidence that this trend is already taking hold.

Revenue in Dell's traditional server segment soared 122% to $10.5 billion in the second quarter. Intel's CPUs help to power many of these servers.

"We are seeing a growing trend of customers that require meaningful CPU compute capacity to support AI and agentic workflows," Dell's chief operating officer, Jeff Clarke, said during the company's Q2 earnings call.

"This is INTC CPUs," Chowdhry said.

title: Mizuho Resets Intel Target For the Rest of 2026
detail:
Mizuho Resets Intel Target For the Rest of 2026
Moz Farooque ACCA
Fri, September 4, 2026 at 3:52 PM EDT 2 min read
INTC
Trade Intel on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Intel (INTC) just received a sharp price-target cut from Mizuho, but the reasoning behind the call is considerably more complicated than a straightforward bearish warning.

Analyst Vijay Rakesh lowered his Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) target to $92 from $109, a reduction of 15.6%, citing near-term multiple compression across agentic AI companies. He retained a Neutral rating, signaling that his concern centers on valuation and sentiment rather than a collapse in Intel's operating outlook.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with INTC.

Is INTC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

INTC GF Value chart

Intel designs CPUs for PCs and data centers while trying to build an external foundry business manufacturing chips for other companies. That mix provides exposure to both traditional hardware refreshes and AI infrastructure, but requires heavy investment and disciplined execution.

Rakesh outlined four tailwinds that could offset the valuation pressure. First, server manufacturers are reporting accelerating agentic AI demand into 2027. Higher token consumption can require more CPUs alongside GPUs, improving the CPU-to-GPU ratio, while conventional enterprise server refreshes add incremental demand.

Second, CPU supply remains constrained. Intel could undership demand through 2027, and major customers may face shortages into next year. Scarcity can support pricing, although it limits how much near-term demand Intel can convert into revenue.

Third, Mizuho estimates Intel's advanced-packaging revenue could reach $3.5 billion by 2029, supported by EMIB-T packaging for tensor processing units. External foundry revenue could separately climb to $3.5 billion as Intel's 14A process ramps.

Finally, PC demand is exceeding expectations as corporate upgrade cycles emerge. Tight memory supply could stretch the refresh cycle, making the recovery steadier rather than short-lived.

For investors, the reduced $92 target captures the tension. Intel has several visible growth levers, but the market may assign lower multiples until foundry execution, supply and AI-driven CPU demand translate into profits. The Neutral rating therefore reflects timing: the opportunity is improving, while confidence in value creation remains incomplete for now.

title: Marvell Stock Had A Huge Year And Still Sits Well Below Its High
detail:
Marvell Stock Had A Huge Year And Still Sits Well Below Its High
Trefis Team

MRVL
INTC
AVGO
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image by Cristian Ibarra from Pixabay

Marvell Technology (MRVL) stock returned 235.9% over the past year, climbing from $62.18 to $208.83. The company kept raising what it expects to sell, and buyers repriced it each time. Then the shares pulled back, and they now sit well below their best.

Marvell Kept Raising What It Says It Will Sell

Marvell finished fiscal 2026 with about $8 billion of revenue, by its CEO's own count. It now guides fiscal 2027 revenue to roughly $12 billion and fiscal 2028 to approximately $18 billion. The fiscal 2028 target rose $1.5 billion in one quarter, from $16.5 billion.

The growth comes from one place. Data centers made up 79% of revenue in fiscal Q2 2027, and management lifted its fiscal 2027 growth outlook for that business to approximately 60% from approximately 50%. Underneath sit the optical DSPs and switching chips that carry traffic between AI accelerators, plus the custom silicon Marvell designs to an individual hyperscaler's specification. Broadcom (AVGO) returned 19.0% over the same window, NVIDIA (NVDA) returned 34.1%, and AMD (AMD) returned 181.4%, a spread wide enough that this wasn't one theme lifting every AI chip stock equally, even as the whole group moved.

But It Is Winning More Work That Carries A Thinner Margin

The custom business is ramping hardest, and it pays least per dollar of sales. Management guided fiscal Q3 2027 non-GAAP gross margin to between 57.5% and 58.5%, down from 58.9% in fiscal Q2 2027, and named the custom ramp as the reason for the step down. The CFO's preliminary view is that fiscal 2028 sits in that same range.

So revenue travels from roughly $12 billion to approximately $18 billion and, from fiscal Q3 2027 on, gross margin does not move. What improves sits lower down. Non-GAAP operating margin widened 180 basis points year over year in fiscal Q2 2027, and management expects that same non-GAAP measure to reach a 38% to 40% target range by fiscal Q4 2027. That comes from operating costs growing slower than revenue.

The newest work shows where that revenue comes from. An expanded agreement with one large hyperscaler covers AI inference accelerators and XPU attach parts: storage controllers, network interface controllers, memory interface controllers. Management says revenue from those programs through fiscal 2028 already sits inside the targets above, and that the programs still ahead will contribute much more significantly in fiscal 2029.

So What Are You Paying For At This Price?

Marvell carries a market capitalization of about $187.4 billion against $9.45 billion of trailing twelve-month revenue, close to 20 times sales. Set that against the approximately $18 billion management expects in fiscal 2028, and it is still over ten times. You are paying for the fiscal 2028 number arriving on schedule and at the margin management described.

title: Dell’s earning report was bullish for Intel CPU demand, analyst says
detail:
Dell’s earning report was bullish for Intel CPU demand, analyst says
Frank DeMatteo
Fri, September 4, 2026 at 11:21 AM EDT 4 min read
INTC
DELL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) could reach $200 per share as surging AI workloads drive what Global Equities Research analyst Trip Chowdhry estimates is 16-fold year-over-year growth in CPU demand. Chowdhry published a note arguing that Dell's most recent earnings call provides direct validation of that thesis, pointing to Dell's traditional server revenue rising 122% year-over-year as evidence of accelerating Intel CPU adoption.

Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) is the most direct equity expression of the structural shift Chowdhry describes. The firm's $200 price target and a 2031 EPS estimate of $20 rest on three interlocking arguments: rising CPU-to-GPU ratios in AI clusters, x86's entrenched enterprise position, and the architectural advantages of Intel's Clearwater Forest processor.

Dell's Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke supplied language that Chowdhry seized on. Clarke said on the earnings call that Dell is seeing "demand for new servers that have more cores" and separately described "a growing trend of customers that require meaningful CPU compute capacity to support AI and agentic workflows." Clarke also noted that traditional server revenue "was up 122% as demand remains exceptionally strong." Chowdhry's note states plainly: "This is INTC CPUs."

The demand driver, in Global Equities Research's telling, is a medium-level shift in AI training workloads. "INTC CPUs are seeing 16x y-y growth as Training shifts to Heavy Media - Video, Images and Audio from simple Text," Chowdhry wrote. Processing video, images, and audio is far more compute-intensive than training on text alone, and CPUs are bearing a growing share of that burden alongside GPUs.

The CPU-to-GPU ratio inversion underpins much of the bull case. Two generations ago, Chowdhry notes, one CPU could manage eight GPUs. Today, according to Global Equities Research, it takes two to four CPUs just to keep pace with a single GPU or TPU. That structural change alone implies a multi-fold increase in CPU unit demand per AI server rack, independent of any market-share gains Intel makes against AMD.

On the competitive landscape, Intel's Clearwater Forest leads the core-count comparison that Chowdhry lays out. Clearwater Forest offers 576 cores, versus AMD's Turin Dense at 192 cores and Nvidia's Vera Rubin at 88 cores, which began shipping in August 2026 per Global Equities Research's summary. Chowdhry frames Nvidia's Vera Rubin and Grace products as "GPU Controllers" rather than true CPU competitors, suggesting the two markets are less head-to-head than commonly assumed.

title: Intel Witnesses an Uptrend in Estimate Revisions: Is it Worth Buying?

Intel Witnesses an Uptrend in Estimate Revisions: Is it Worth Buying?
Aritra Chatterjee
Fri, September 4, 2026 at 10:57 AM EDT 4 min read
INTC

Trading disclosure

Earnings estimates for Intel Corporation INTC for 2026 and 2027 have moved up 44.12% to $1.47 and 35.42% to $1.95, respectively, over the past 60 days. The positive estimate revisions depict bullish sentiments about the stock's growth potential.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

INTC Rides on Strong AI Traction, Improving Manufacturing Execution

Data Center and AI (DCAI) is emerging as one of Intel's strongest growth engines for the company. DCAI revenue increased 59% year over year to $6.3 billion in the second quarter, supported by strong demand from hyperscale and enterprise customers. Strong server CPU demand and growing adoption of Xeon 6 processors are expected to fuel growth in upcoming quarters.

Intel is rapidly broadening its traditional PC offerings by incorporating AI capabilities. AI PC revenues are up 26% sequentially and represent about two-thirds of segment revenues. At Hot Chips 2026, Intel detailed Wildcat Lake, launched as Intel Core Series 3, for laptops and intelligent edge platforms. Built on Intel 18A, it combines CPU cores, Xe3 graphics with XMX acceleration and an NPU delivering up to 17 TOPS, while marking Intel's first use of UCIe in a processor. Intel has secured 130 Series 3 edge AI design wins, and edge deployments account for 10% of CCPG revenue.

Intel is expanding beyond general-purpose CPUs into customized silicon designed for specific workloads. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, purpose-built silicon revenue increased about 20% sequentially and nearly tripled year over year, reaching an estimated $2 billion run rate, with management targeting $4 billion in the not-too-distant future.

Operational improvements are providing another potential earnings driver. Intel is seeing better yields, faster cycle times and higher factory output across several process nodes. In the second quarter, higher revenue, improved yields and pricing contributed to a non-GAAP gross margin of 41.8%, while operating cash flow reached $7 billion.

Supply Constraints, Stiff Competition, Weak PC Market are Concerns

Intel is dealing with a difficult supply environment even as demand remains strong. Industry-wide shortages of leading-edge wafers, memory and substrates are limiting the company's ability to fully capitalize on the growing customer requirements. Management expects PC consumption to decline at a low-double-digit rate in 2026, citing higher memory prices and supply constraints.

Intel operates in an industry characterized by aggressive competition and rapid technological change. It faces competition from Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Arm Holdings ARM in server CPUs. The broader AI infrastructure market remains highly contested across CPUs, GPUs, ASICs and networking. Intel's confidence in catching up and later leapfrogging competitors depends on timely execution across Clearwater Forest, Diamond Rapids and Coral Rapids.

Intel's global manufacturing and supply chain expose it to geopolitical and trade-related risks. The company specifically highlights tensions involving the United States and China, developments around Taiwan, tariffs and export controls as factors that could disrupt operations.

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $517.91, leading the market. The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 0.02% to $718.70, representing a tiny fraction of the chip move.

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) is one of the loudest names inside that rotation. Intel stock is up 4% to $95.41 in early trading, extending a year-long run built on the foundry turnaround thesis. The move stands out because it's happening on a session when the macro backdrop should be working against high-multiple chip names.

Jobs Beat Lifts Rate Hike Odds

The Labor Department reported that employers added 162,000 jobs in August, well above the 65,000 economists had penciled in, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. According to CME FedWatch, expectations for a September rate hike jumped to 60.2% from 49.4% on Thursday.

Intel announced no company-specific news this morning. The move reads as sector flow rather than a fresh catalyst, and higher rates would typically pressure rate-sensitive semiconductor valuations first. That the chip group is bid anyway suggests capital is rotating specifically into semiconductors while the broader risk-on tape lags.
